issue.title: Feature Request: Optional API-backed Google engine (no HTML scraping)

relevant_locations.role: Defines the SearchEngine trait implemented by search engines
Instantiates and registers search engines into the application vector

llm_context.input_title: Feature Request: Optional API-backed Google engine (no HTML scraping)
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: The repository currently implements HTML-scraping engines (DuckDuckGo, Brave, Startpage, Yahoo) that are prone to selector breakage and IP rate-limiting, alongside a fragile internal Google Images API. This issue proposes adding an optional, API-backed Google web search engine (using SerpBase) that activates only when an API key is provided via an environment variable, leaving existing behavior unchanged.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The metasearch engine architecture relies on a `SearchEngine` trait implemented by individual engine modules and explicitly wired into `src/main.rs` and `src/engines/mod.rs`. Without a dedicated SerpBase engine implementation, module declaration, and conditional instantiation in `main.rs`, the API-backed Google option cannot participate in the aggregator RRF pipeline.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect SearchEngine trait and existing engine implementations
step_by_step_plan.description: Examine the SearchEngine trait defined in src/engines/mod.rs and reference existing engine implementations such as startpage.rs to understand asynchronous request handling and response parsing conventions.

step_by_step_plan.title: Implement the SerpBase engine module
step_by_step_plan.description: Create src/engines/serpbase.rs implementing the SearchEngine trait, fetching results from the SerpBase API when SERPBASE_API_KEY is present in the environment.

step_by_step_plan.title: Register SerpBase engine in src/engines/mod.rs and src/main.rs
step_by_step_plan.description: Expose the serpbase module in src/engines/mod.rs and conditionally instantiate and push the SerpBase engine into the search engine vector in src/main.rs based on the SERPBASE_API_KEY environment variable.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add integration and unit tests for SerpBase engine
step_by_step_plan.description: Add unit tests verifying that the SerpBase engine correctly handles missing API keys without error and successfully parses mock API responses when configured.

step_by_step_plan.title: Execute test suite
step_by_step_plan.description: Run cargo test to verify that all existing engines and the new SerpBase engine pass successfully without regressions.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: A Rust trait defining a common interface (name and async search method returning a list of search results) that allows different search backends to be treated uniformly.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: It decouples the core aggregation logic from specific search providers, making it trivial to plug in new search backends.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Implementing a new SerpBase engine requires adhering to this exact trait so it can be seamlessly passed into `query_all_engines()`.

structured_concepts.concept_name: Optional Feature Activation via Environment Variables
structured_concepts.short_explanation: Conditional initialization of features based on whether required configuration secrets or API keys are present in the environment.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Allows third-party API integrations to remain completely optional, preserving self-hosted privacy and preventing crashes when keys are missing.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: The SerpBase engine should only be instantiated and added to the engine fan-out if `SERPBASE_API_KEY` is set.

common_pitfalls: Modifying the core RRF aggregator or existing engine scrapers when only a new engine module is needed.
Failing to check for the presence of the `SERPBASE_API_KEY` environment variable, causing unexpected failures when the key is absent.
